syllabus_version.title: CBSE Curriculum for the Academic Year 2026-27

book.title: Vistas
book.edition: NCERT (reprint year not stated in the prelims)

topics.title: Charley's claim and the psychiatrist's diagnosis

concepts.learning_objective: Recall Charley's claim that Grand Central has a third level and who denies it.
Explain the psychiatrist's view that the third level is a waking-dream wish fulfilment born of modern anxiety.
Evaluate Charley's response to the idea that his stamp collecting is a refuge from reality.

topics.title: Lost in Grand Central: reaching the third level

concepts.learning_objective: Recall how Charley, heading for the subway, wandered into corridors that led to the third level.
Interpret Charley's image of Grand Central growing like a tree and serving as a way of escape.
Identify the details of dress, lighting and the newspaper that told Charley he was in 1894.

topics.title: The dream of Galesburg and the ticket window

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why Charley longed to take Louisa to the peaceful Galesburg of 1894.
Explain why the clerk rejected Charley's money and what Charley did with old-style currency afterwards.

topics.title: The first-day cover and Sam's letter

concepts.learning_objective: Define a first-day cover and explain how its postmark dates Sam's letter.
Infer from Sam's letter what has happened to him and how it changes Charley and Louisa.
Analyse the effect of the final revelation that Sam was Charley's psychiatrist.

topics.title: Author, narration and themes: escape, time and fantasy

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the author of the story and its first-person narrator.
Evaluate the story's treatment of the human wish to escape the stress of modern life.
Analyse how the story interweaves fantasy and reality through an intersection of time and space.

topics.title: The narrator, the royal titles and the prophecy at birth

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the narrator's mock-heroic tone and the king's string of grand titles set up the story's satire.
Recall the astrologers' prediction about the prince's death and interpret the infant's reaction to it.

topics.title: Upbringing, coming of age and the astrologer's warning

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the crown prince's English upbringing and explain what it satirises.
State the astrologer's warning about the hundredth tiger and explain how it shapes the Maharaja's mission.

topics.title: The ban on tiger hunting and the British officer

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why the Maharaja banned tiger hunting for everyone else and the irony in calling it a celebration for the tigers.
Interpret the episode of the British officer and the diamond rings as a comment on power and bribery.

topics.title: Tigers run out and the Maharaja's marriage

concepts.learning_objective: Recall how the tiger population of Pratibandapuram ended and interpret the narrator's humour about it.
Evaluate how the Maharaja turns his marriage into a means of reaching his tally of tigers.

topics.title: The hunt for the hundredth tiger

concepts.learning_objective: Analyse how the Maharaja's obsession with the hundredth tiger makes him harsh towards his officers and subjects.
Describe the dewan's plan to supply an old tiger and explain what it reveals about the hunt.
Explain why the hunters hid the Maharaja's missed shot and how this sets up the ending.

topics.title: The wooden tiger and the Maharaja's death

concepts.learning_objective: Recall the episode of the wooden tiger bought for the crown prince and explain the satire on autocratic rule in it.
Explain how the wooden tiger becomes the 'hundredth tiger' that fulfils the prophecy.

topics.title: Satire, dramatic irony and the story's message

concepts.learning_objective: Evaluate the story as a satire on the conceit of those in power and on the fearful flattery of their followers.
Identify instances of dramatic irony in the story and explain their effect.
Interpret the author's indirect comment on the cruelty of human beings towards wild animals.

chapters.title: Journey to the end of the Earth

topics.title: The journey to Antarctica and first impressions

concepts.learning_objective: Recall the vessel, route and duration of the writer's journey to Antarctica and what these details convey.
Explain the relief and wonder the writer felt on first facing Antarctica's landscape.

topics.title: Part of history: Gondwana and the shaping of the globe

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the Gondwana supercontinent and how it broke up into the continents we know.
Explain how geological events such as the forming of the Himalayas and the Drake Passage shaped the present globe.

topics.title: Human impact and the climate change debate

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how human populations and fossil-fuel burning have affected Nature and global temperature.
Explain why Antarctica is crucial to the study of climate change and the Earth's past and future.

topics.title: Students on Ice and the parable of the phytoplankton

concepts.learning_objective: State the aims of the Students on Ice programme and Geoff Green's reasons for taking high school students.
Interpret the role of phytoplankton and the lesson 'take care of the small things and the big things will fall into place'.

topics.title: Walk on the ocean and the closing reflection

concepts.learning_objective: Recall the walk on the ice pack and interpret the writer's realisation that everything connects.
Interpret the writer's closing reflection on the balance of the planet and the hope offered by the young.

topics.title: Dr Sadao's background and the man from the sea

concepts.learning_objective: Students recall Dr Sadao's upbringing, education, marriage and why he was kept in Japan during the war.
Students describe how Sadao and Hana found the wounded man and identified him as an escaped American prisoner of war.

topics.title: The dilemma: doctor or patriot

concepts.learning_objective: Students explain the conflict between Sadao's duty as a doctor and his loyalty as a Japanese citizen.
Students interpret the servants' superstitious and patriotic reactions to the enemy in the house.

topics.title: The operation and Hana's role

concepts.learning_objective: Students explain how Hana overcame fear and dislike to wash the prisoner and give the anaesthetic.
Students analyse how Sadao's training and absorption in surgery override his hostility to the patient.

topics.title: The household under pressure

concepts.learning_objective: Students describe how the servants' disapproval and departure put pressure on Sadao and Hana.
Students analyse the uncertainty Sadao and Hana feel about what they ought to do with the prisoner.

topics.title: The General and the plan to kill the prisoner

concepts.learning_objective: Students evaluate the General's attitude to Sadao and the prisoner as one of self-absorption.
Students recall the General's offer of private assassins and how Sadao responded to it.

topics.title: The escape and the meaning of the story

concepts.learning_objective: Students recall how Sadao arranged the prisoner's escape and the signals he asked for.
Students evaluate how the ending shows humanity rising above hatred and prejudice.

topics.title: Derry enters Mr Lamb's garden (Scene One, opening)

concepts.learning_objective: Recall how and why Derry comes into Mr Lamb's garden and how the two first meet.
Explain how Derry's acid-burned face has made him fearful, defensive and withdrawn.

topics.title: Mr Lamb's view of difference: weeds, the tin leg and Beauty and the Beast

concepts.learning_objective: Interpret Mr Lamb's comparison of weeds and flowers as a lesson that all life has equal worth.
Describe how Mr Lamb lives calmly with his tin leg and the mockery it brings.
Analyse Derry's rejection of the Beauty and the Beast story and Mr Lamb's reply that the world has a whole face.

topics.title: Hurtful words, fear and hatred

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how Mr Lamb questions the power Derry gives to cruel remarks he has overheard.
Interpret the story of the man who locked himself away as a lesson about fear and isolation.
Explain why Mr Lamb says hatred does more harm than acid.

topics.title: Friendship, the open gate and Mr Lamb's loneliness

concepts.learning_objective: Explain what the open gate, the curtainless windows and Mr Lamb's idea of friendship show about him.
Identify the signs of loneliness and disappointment in Mr Lamb at the end of Scene One.
Analyse how Derry's attitude towards Mr Lamb changes by the end of Scene One.

topics.title: Scene Two: Derry and his mother

concepts.learning_objective: Describe Derry's mother's fears and her attempt to keep him at home.
Explain Derry's new resolve to return to the garden and to the world.

topics.title: Scene Three: the ending and the meaning of the title

concepts.learning_objective: Recall and interpret the events and the irony of the play's final scene.
Evaluate how the title and the bond between Derry and Mr Lamb express the play's theme.

topics.title: Introduction: the two writers and their works

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the two writers, their communities and the focus of the unit.
Explain the meaning and the pun in the title 'Karukku'.

topics.title: Zitkala-Sa: the first day at school
topics.ncert_sections: I. The Cutting of My Long Hair (the dining room)

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how the strange school surroundings and dress affected Zitkala-Sa.
Explain the bell-controlled breakfast and why she calls it 'eating by formula'.

topics.title: Zitkala-Sa: the cutting of her long hair
topics.ncert_sections: I. The Cutting of My Long Hair (the haircut)

concepts.learning_objective: Explain what long and shingled hair meant among Zitkala-Sa's people.
Analyse Zitkala-Sa's resistance and her sense of humiliation when her hair is cut.

topics.title: Bama: the walk home and the elder with the vadais
topics.ncert_sections: II. We Too are Human Beings (the bazaar and the threshing floor)

concepts.learning_objective: Recall the sights that delayed Bama and explain why she describes them so fully.
Interpret the scene of the elder carrying the packet to the landlord.

topics.title: Bama: Annan's explanation and advice
topics.ncert_sections: II. We Too are Human Beings (Annan's words)

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how Annan reveals the practice of untouchability to Bama.
Evaluate Annan's advice that study can help throw away indignities.

topics.title: Comparing the two accounts

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the common theme of the two accounts from distant cultures.
Compare the kinds of discrimination the two girls face and their responses.
